column3: The Hebrew explicitly mentions processions in the plural; BSB describes one choir proceeding.
The Hebrew explicitly says they went after them; BSB says they followed without repeating that object.
The Hebrew calls them sons of the priests; BSB says some of the priests.
The Hebrew calls them his brothers and refers to David’s musical instruments without a separate word for prescribed; BSB says associates and instruments prescribed by David.
The Hebrew says singers rather than choirs and separately names Jezrahiah as overseer; BSB describes choirs singing under his direction.
The Hebrew says the priests and Levites were standing; BSB interprets this as serving.
The Hebrew repeats the root of guarding for keeping God’s charge; BSB says performing His service.
The Hebrew gives song in the singular; BSB gives songs in the plural.
The Hebrew specifies the daily portions for singers and gatekeepers, then speaks of consecrating for Levites and sons of Aaron; BSB repeats daily portions for these later groups as well.
